Query Supabase as the signed-in user

Source: R/backend__supabase.R
oauth_db_supabase_api.Rd

Read tables and views, call database functions, or send native Data API requests with the visitor's access token. Supabase applies the database's grants and row-level security policies.

Usage

oauth_db_supabase_api(
  authorization,
  url,
  api_key,
  schema = NULL,
  target = NULL,
  required_scopes = character(),
  min_valid_for = 60,
  timeout = 30,
  ca_bundle = NULL,
  session = shiny::getDefaultReactiveDomain()
)

Arguments

authorization

auth$connection from a shinyOAuth server module, without parentheses. To select a saved authorization, pass a function that calls auth$connection(id).

url

HTTPS Supabase project base URL, without /rest/v1 or /auth/v1. Custom domains and reverse proxy paths are supported.

api_key

Project publishable key (sb_publishable_...) or legacy anon JWT. Secret and service_role keys are rejected.

schema

Exposed PostgreSQL schema, or NULL for the server default.

target

Token target name in the shinyOAuth client. NULL uses its default token, including for clients without named targets.

required_scopes

Additional permissions to check before use. Request consent and set the client's permission requirements in shinyOAuth.

min_valid_for

Minimum remaining token lifetime, in seconds, when obtaining a token. Use 0 to accept any unexpired token.

timeout

Maximum seconds for one request, including its refresh retry.

ca_bundle

Optional path to a trusted CA certificate bundle.

session

Shiny session. Inferred when the helper is created in server().

Value

An R6 client with the same select(), rpc(), and request() methods as oauth_db_postgrest_api(). select() returns a data frame; rpc() and request() return the parsed JSON value, or an httr2 response with raw = TRUE.

Details

Create the client inside server(). Each request sends the project key in apikey and the visitor's current access token in Authorization. The project key is never used as a substitute for a missing user token. No database password or PostgreSQL driver is needed.

Use oauth_db_supabase_client() with Supabase's OAuth server, or supply an authorization from a third-party provider trusted by the project. OAuth scopes do not grant table access; configure database grants and RLS. This helper accesses the REST Data API, not SQL connections, Storage, Realtime, or the Management API.

The underlying PostgREST client obtains a current token for each operation, discards responses after account changes or sign-out, and retries GET/HEAD once after HTTP 401. Writes and POST function calls are never replayed. Verified HTTPS is required, including for self-hosted deployments.

See also

oauth_db_supabase_client(), oauth_db_postgrest_api(). vignette("supabase", package = "shinyOAuthDB") has setup instructions and a complete Shiny app.

Other platform API clients: oauth_db_bigquery_api(), oauth_db_clickhouse_api(), oauth_db_cratedb_api(), oauth_db_databricks_api(), oauth_db_fabric_api(), oauth_db_libsql_api(), oauth_db_opensearch_api(), oauth_db_oracle_ords_api(), oauth_db_postgrest_api(), oauth_db_salesforce_api(), oauth_db_salesforce_data_cloud_api()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
supabase <- oauth_db_supabase_api(auth$connection,
  url = Sys.getenv("OAUTHDB_SUPABASE_URL"),
  api_key = Sys.getenv("OAUTHDB_SUPABASE_KEY"))
output$rows <- shiny::renderTable({
  supabase$select("orders", order = "id.asc", limit = 20L)
})
} # }
